timeline.question: How quickly can you build our platform?
timeline.answer: It depends on scope, but here is how we approach timelines. We break everything into weekly sprints with live demos, so you see real progress every week instead of vague updates. Most platforms launch in phases: core features first (usually 8 to 12 weeks), then we iterate and add more based on what you learn from real users. You get a clear roadmap after our first conversation.

involvement.question: How involved will we be during development?
involvement.answer: Very. Every week you see what has been built, test it live, and give feedback that shapes the next sprint. This is not a disappear-for-months-then-surprise-you situation. You are part of the process from day one.

integrations.question: Can you integrate with our existing tools?
integrations.answer: Yes. Payment gateways, CRMs, email platforms, Zoom, Google Meet, SSO, whatever you currently use gets connected. We build around your workflow, not against it.

afterLaunch.question: What happens after we launch?
afterLaunch.answer: Launch is the beginning, not the end. We offer optional maintenance contracts for ongoing support, updates, new features, and optimizations. Most clients stay with us long-term because their platform keeps evolving with their needs.

scale.question: Will the platform scale as we grow?
scale.answer: That is the plan. We architect for growth from day one. Whether you are at 500 learners or 50,000, the infrastructure supports it, and we adjust as you scale.

mobile.question: Is the platform mobile-friendly?
mobile.answer: Completely. It works on desktop, tablet, and mobile, responsive by default rather than as an afterthought.

ownership.question: Who owns the code and platform?
ownership.answer: You do. Full ownership transfers to you on final payment: the code, the platform, the infrastructure. Maintenance is optional, never required.

lmsAlternativesPage.h1: LMS alternatives, without pretending every team needs a custom build.
lmsAlternativesPage.sub: A hosted or open-source LMS is often the right choice. Build custom software when the platform itself is part of your offer, your operations, or your edge.

worthIt.question: When is a custom LMS worth it?
worthIt.answer: When your learning experience, business rules, data, or integrations are important enough that fixed product settings create recurring manual work or lost opportunities.

replaceWorking.question: Should we replace an LMS that already works?
replaceWorking.answer: Usually no. Keep a working LMS when its constraints are tolerable and its operating model suits your team. Replace it when the constraints affect a core part of your programme or product.

stages.question: Can we migrate in stages?
stages.answer: Yes. A staged migration can move one programme, audience, or workflow first. It reduces risk and makes the lessons from the first release useful before a broader cutover.

bottomCta.title: Bring the awkward workflow to the call.
bottomCta.description: We will help you sort a practical upgrade from a platform replacement. Sometimes the right answer is to keep what you have.

hero.intro1: I'm Choaib Mouhrach, founder of Rizon and a software engineer specializing in learning technology. For the past several years I've worked almost exclusively on LMS development, building custom learning platforms and integrating systems like Moodle, Canvas, and LTI for education businesses and training organizations.
hero.intro2: I started Rizon to give organizations an alternative to forcing their workflows into off-the-shelf platforms.

aboutRizon.title: Learning platforms built around how your organization already operates.
aboutRizon.p1: Rizon is a software studio focused exclusively on learning platforms. We design and build custom LMS products for education businesses, training companies, schools, and organizations whose current platform no longer fits how they operate.
aboutRizon.p2: That includes everything from complete learning platforms to Moodle and Canvas development, LTI integrations, assessment systems, reporting, course commerce, and internal training portals.
aboutRizon.p3: Every project starts with understanding how your organization teaches and operates, then building software around that instead of forcing your team to adapt to generic LMS software.

small.title: Small releases

direct.title: Direct conversations

code.title: Code you keep
